title_prefix: ms-from-script has no tapscript arms: no
mechanism: MS-FROM-SCRIPT's SINGLE_BKV_EXPR key arm tests only (eql 33 (%ms-op-push-size ops in)) (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1800), so a 32-byte x-only push is not a key, and the whole decoder (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1752-1994) has no OP_NUMEQUAL / OP_CHECKSIGADD arm at all -- +ms-op-checksigadd+ is named only by script GENERATION (miniscript.lisp:552), never by the decoder. A tapscript leaf therefore falls through to the closing (t (fail)) at its first key push. Core's DecodeScript accepts in[0].second.size() == 33 || == 32 as a key (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:2326-2332) and has a dedicated MULTI_A arm (miniscript.h:2394-2420) that walks the <x> CHECKSIG (<x> CHECKSIGADD)* <k> OP_NUMEQUAL chain backwards, bounds it by MAX_PUBKEYS_PER_MULTI_A = 999 (refs/bitcoin/src/script/script.h:37) and std::reverse-s the collected keys; the same arm rejects MULTI when IsTapscript and MULTI_A when not. MS-FROM-SCRIPT also takes no context argument (defun ms-from-script (script)), so it silently inherits whatever *ms-context* is bound to; both shipped callers leave it at the :p2wsh default.
consequence: Latent today, and confirmed latent by grep: MS-FROM-SCRIPT has exactly two callers in src/ -- src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:469 (Core's P2WSH miniscript signing arm, reached with a witnessScript) and src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:489 (P2WSH satisfaction sizing). Neither ever supplies a tapscript leaf, so nothing is currently mis-signed, mis-sized or wrongly accepted. The divergence is a bounded inference gap: S3 stands. Its importance is ordering, not severity -- it is a hard blocker for the S1 1141db2b fix, whose Core-faithful shape (SignTaprootScript, refs/bitcoin/src/script/sign.cpp:528-540) is literally FromScript(leaf_script, TapSatisfier) followed by Satisfy. Executed here: EVERY tapscript leaf that contains a key -- which is every leaf a wallet would ever spend -- infers NIL today, so a straight port of SignTaprootScript on top of the current decoder would sign nothing and report the same 'complete: false' the S1 already produces. It also blocks Core's InferScript taproot-leaf arm (refs/bitcoin/src/script/descriptor.cpp:2806-2816), which we do not have.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-miniscript-s3, warm image, probe build/ga11probe/p1.lisp (git-ignored) run twice with identical results. Each case parses an expression in one context, takes ms-node-script, and feeds those exact bytes back to ms-from-script under the same *ms-context*. Results (label ctx -> inferred): pk :TAPSCRIPT script 20d30199..ac -> NIL; pk :P2WSH script 2103d30199..ac -> 'pk(03d30199..)'; multi_a(1,K1,K2) :TAPSCRIPT script 20d30199..ac20fff97b..ba519c -> NIL; multi(1,K1,K2) :P2WSH -> 'multi(1,03d30199..,03fff97b..)'; older(100) :TAPSCRIPT -> 'older(100)' and :P2WSH -> 'older(100)'. The older() rows are the positive control: tapscript inference is not broken as a whole, only the two arms that read a key. pkh :TAPSCRIPT -> 'pkh(2146bb25abba6eae79456c8cc95cca17919e9aeb)' decodes structurally (the 20-byte hash arm is context-free) but carries no key, which is the separate finding c7fe77bf. Core side read at d3056bc: miniscript.h:2326-2332 (32-or-33-byte key push), :2394-2420 (MULTI_A), script.h:37 (MAX_PUBKEYS_PER_MULTI_A 999), and refs/bitcoin/src/test/miniscript_tests.cpp:467-469, where Test() asserts 'Cannot infer miniscript from script' plus a byte-exact round trip for EVERY vector in BOTH contexts (miniscript_tests.cpp:485-489 runs each vector through wsh_converter and tap_converter) -- so Core's own suite would fail on our decoder. Ours: src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1752 (defun, no ctx parameter), :1800 (the 33-only key test), :552 (the only mention of +ms-op-checksigadd+), and the two call sites src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:469, src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:489.
fix_shape: Port the two missing DecodeScript arms and give ms-from-script an explicit context. Change the key test at miniscript.lisp:1800 from (eql 33 ...) to (member (%ms-op-push-size ops in) '(32 33)), matching miniscript.h:2326 -- the size check is Core's only key gate, and *ms-context* already drives how ms-node-script re-serialises the key, so the round trip closes on its own. Then add a MULTI_A arm next to the existing :multi arm, gated on (eq *ms-context* :tapscript) and triggered by +ms-op-numequal+ at op 0: read k with %ms-op-number at op 1, refuse k < 1 or k > +ms-max-pubkeys-per-multi-a+ (999, already defined at miniscript.lisp:126), then walk pairs from pos 2 in steps of 2 requiring OP_CHECKSIGADD or OP_CHECKSIG at pos and a 32-byte push at pos+1, stopping at the OP_CHECKSIG that ends the chain, refusing more than 999 keys and fewer than k, and advancing in by 2 + 2*nkeys. Because the decoder already walks the script backwards, the keys come off in Core's post-std::reverse order -- assert that against a generated multi_a(2,K1,K2,K3) script rather than assuming it. Also add the symmetric guards Core has: refuse MULTI under :tapscript (miniscript.h:2375) and MULTI_A outside it (:2397). Finally give ms-from-script a (script &key (ctx *ms-context*)) lambda list that binds *ms-context* for the whole decode, so the tr() caller cannot inherit :p2wsh by accident. Verify with Core's own oracle: replay the 91 miniscript_tests.cpp Test() vectors in both contexts and require FromScript non-NIL plus a byte-exact re-serialisation for all 182 runs. This must land BEFORE 1141db2b.
